title: Web Accessibility Basics Every Dev Should Know
intro: Accessible sites work for everyone, including people using screen readers, keyboards or zoom.

slides.heading: Alt text
slides.subtitle: Describe your images.
points: Screen readers read alt text aloud
Describe the purpose, not just the look
Use alt="" for purely decorative images

slides.heading: Keyboard access
slides.subtitle: Not everyone uses a mouse.
points: Everything clickable works with Tab and Enter

slides.heading: Color contrast
slides.subtitle: Make text easy to read.
points: WCAG AA asks for 4.5:1 for normal text
Don't rely on color alone to show meaning

slides.heading: Forms
slides.subtitle: Where accessibility breaks most often.
points: Error messages should say how to fix it
Placeholder text is not a label

scenario.situation: A checkout form uses grey placeholder text instead of labels.
scenario.problem: Screen reader users can't tell what each field is, and the hint disappears as soon as anyone types.
scenario.fix: Add a visible <label for="email"> to every input, and keep placeholders for examples only.
scenario.takeaway: Every input needs a real label.

cta: Have you ever tried using your site with only a keyboard?
